newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian monetary bodies say no news conference.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian monetary bodies say no news conference.

text.p: Indonesian officials said on Tuesday there was no news conference scheduled during the day following market rumours of a possible announcement of new rules which could affect the foreign exchange market.
The rupiah fell through the 3,000 barrier to a low of 3,045 to the dollar and swap rates rose sharply on fears that the government was planning to announce new measures.

Dealers said the worries resulted from comments by the Coordinating Minister for Economics, Finance and Supervisor of Development Saleh Afiff that liquidity tightening was now the "homework" of the finance minister and central bank governor.
"I cannot explain how the further tightening will be carried out. Because it will be done tomorrow (Tuesday)," he was quoted by the Bisnis Indonesia daily as saying.
However, officials at the finance ministry, the coordinating ministry and the central bank said there was no news conference scheduled for Tuesday.
Currency dealers said rumours of a news conference on Tuesday sent the rupiah to a new low before it recovered to the 3,000 level, with sentiment seen mixed.
